title: orch automation ticket data: ext.automation
description: Owned by the automation add-on (its ticket_ext; the add-on ships a byte-identical copy). The core never reads it. One-time waits stay core: waiting_on {kind: time, until}. A repeating ticket has recurring/cron/tz/agent/each_run/last_run; a sub-ticket made for one run (each_run = sub-ticket) has run/at/occurrence.

paused.description: true = the repeat is switched off: it stays listed but does not start runs. Absent = on.

recurring.description: true = run again and again by cron.

cron.description: 5-field cron (min hour day month weekday), read in tz (UTC when tz is absent). Missed runs (machine off): one catch-up run, never several.

tz.description: IANA time zone the cron is read in, e.g. Europe/Zurich. Default: [workspace] tz of .orch/config.toml, else UTC.

agent.description: Names an agent: a built-in adapter or an [agents.<name>] entry of .orch/config.toml. Never a command. Default: [workspace] agent.

each_run.description: Optional. Each run gets its own sub-ticket (parent = this ticket); only for repeats daily or slower (cron minute and hour are plain numbers, checked here). Absent = every run works on this ticket.

last_run.description: Written by the add-on after each run.

run.description: On a sub-ticket: made for one run of its parent.

at.description: On a sub-ticket: the planned time of that run (UTC).

occurrence.description: On a sub-ticket: <parent id>:<at>. One sub-ticket per occurrence; a crashed tick finds it and reuses it.

cron.description: each_run needs a repeat daily or slower: one fixed minute and hour.
